## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `60981028c1462e71f9b72f08ef312e4c0c0d98d8`
Local-runs: none

PR #37485 (card #37365, epic #36996 row 10b). Declaration face: the paths decide no face, the changeset's `Clause-②: yes` does. Read: the card body and its five comments (triage 7177776258, unblock 7182901366, claim 7182933721, os-dev report 7186618419, claim amendment 7186643284), the PR body, `git diff origin/main...pr-37485` (27 files, +1050/−14, merge base `5d21d431e`), the head's check-runs, card #37487, ADR-0160 D3/D9 and `record-body-anchor.ts` / `record-citation.zod.ts` on `main` (`4925039a75`). Nothing was built or run; every finding below is a reading of the code, and none was reproduced.

### ① Derived judgments

**Verdict in one line:** no must-fix. Four should-fix, five nits. The security questions come out clean; the "never a wrong heading" claim does not hold as written (S1).

**1. Security and leaks: clean.**
- Where a chip can navigate. `recordOpenTarget` (`AiChatPage.tsx`) builds a fixed `/apps/APP/OBJ/record/ID` path, each segment through `encodeURIComponent`, and the anchor through `URLSearchParams`. The string always starts with `/apps/` and goes to the router's `navigate`, so no scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`), no host and no protocol-relative form can be produced: no open redirect. The anchor cannot leave the query string. One residue is N1 below (dot segments).
- The anchor and the DOM. The `section` value is only compared with `===` against the anchors `headingsOf` derives (`sectionCandidates`). It is never put in a selector, an attribute, an id or markup. The one selector built (`locateSection`) interpolates a field NAME taken from the object's metadata, not from the URL, with `"` and `\` escaped. The mark is a fixed attribute and fixed classes. The chip draws `quote` as React text and a `title` attribute. No injection path found.
- Reading rights. The chip only navigates; the record route does its ordinary read. `sectionCandidates` runs only once `holdsRouteRecord` is true, on `readablePageRecord`, so it sees only what the page already holds for this user; a field the user is not served is absent and yields no candidate. Nothing is fetched or verified on display (ruling Q1), and no endpoint is added.
- The part is read through `RecordCitationsSchema.safeParse` (strict object, max 20); a refused part or an empty list draws nothing. The ablation in the PR body covers that gate.
- `Security-touching: no`: no changed hunk changes or teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour.

**2. `section` as a reserved param: holds.** `RECORD_SECTION_PARAM = 'section'` is declared in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/urlParams.ts`, the one registry, in the param table and in `RESERVED_URL_PARAMS`, and pinned in `recordSectionAnchor.test.tsx`. On `main` no reader or writer uses `section` as a query parameter in `ui/` or `packages/` (the hits are component types, HTML tags and JSX props). The reader imports the constant; no literal. The writer is the chat opener alone.

**3. Point (a), the heading locator.**

S1 (should-fix) — `locateSection` can mark a wrong heading, so "falls back to the field, never to a wrong heading" is false as written. `ordinal` counts earlier headings of the OUTLINE that read the same; the index is then applied to the DRAWN headings that read the same. The two sets differ exactly where A2 failed, and when the differing heading reads the same as the cited one, the index lands on it:
- Drawn but not listed, before the cited one. Body: a setext `Scope` heading, then `# Scope`. The outline lists one heading, anchor `scope`, ordinal 0. The face draws two that read `scope`; index 0 is the setext one. The same holds for `> # Scope` in a quote, a heading in a list item, and an ATX heading indented one to three spaces (CommonMark draws it; `markdownHeadingOf` counts `#` from column 0 and does not list it).
- Listed but not drawn. A `# Scope` line inside a block the face does not draw as a heading (a raw HTML block; a four-backtick fence whose inner three-backtick line `isFence` reads as a close) takes anchor `scope`, and the real later heading takes `scope-2`. Citing `scope` marks the real heading; citing `scope-2` falls to the field.
- A heading with no letter or digit (anchor `section-N`) has the reading `""`, which also matches every empty heading the face draws.
Two different headings that merely normalise alike (`C` and `C++`, `Re-scope` and `Rescope`) do resolve correctly, since the same reading orders both sides; the fault needs the sets to differ. It is rare, and the heading reached carries the same title. Smallest fix: carry the outline's same-reading count on the candidate and open at the field when the drawn same-reading count differs; add the setext-duplicate case as a pin. Until then the PR body and the report should not say "never".

S2 (should-fix) — a second citation of the same record leaves the first mark on. `focusRecordSection`'s cleanup disconnects and clears the timer but never removes `data-record-section-target` or the mark classes. With the dock beside the record, clicking chip A (`scope`) and then chip B (`scope-2`) changes `citedSectionKey` on a mounted `RecordDetailView` whose body is not redrawn, so both headings stay marked. Several citations of one record is the ordinary case. The cleanup should unmark. A related gap: clicking the same chip again after scrolling away does nothing, because the key is unchanged.

Accepted as disclosed: the body is the first long-text field in field order whose outline issues the anchor, not the pack's `body.field` (the URL carries no `context`). ADR-0160 D9 leaves "how a surface opens the root record at `anchor`" to row 10, so this is the PR's to decide.

**4. Point (b), surface beyond the claim: acceptable.** The report lists the extra files under `deviations`, the PR body under acceptance notes, and claim amendment 7186643284 records them on the card. The dispatch shape is "stop on breach; explain in the report"; the dev explained and did not stop, and the amendment came after the push (N5). Each addition is the smallest that works: one attribute on the two detail row faces, one key on `RuntimeOnlyMessageKeys`, the helper and its test, two doc pages. `data-detail-field` collides with no existing attribute (`data-detail-field-row` and `-label` are distinct names). Overlap with #37436 (open, head `116e0426e9`): its `DetailSection.tsx` hunks are at lines 35 and 648, this PR's at 952 and 979; it also edits all 11 locale files, near line 200, against this PR's near line 4700 and later. Disjoint hunks in every shared file, either merge order.

**5. Points (c) and (d).**
- (d) verified with git. `git diff e581d1410..60981028c` touches five files: the changeset, `plugin-chatbot.mdx`, the chatbot `README.md`, `recordSectionAnchor.ts` (three lines: the `let timer` became a `const pending` holder) and `RecordCitations.tsx` (one line: `export` dropped from `recordCitationTarget`). The claim is exact. It is also moot: the head's own CI ran the full suites (Test UI 16/16 shards, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, all success).
- Check-runs on the head: 62 completed, 52 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, as the area reports.

S4 (should-fix) — the browser reading is NOT MEASURED and has no carrier. The substitute (the real `RecordDetailView` with the real markdown face in jsdom, `scrollIntoView` stubbed) proves which element is chosen. It does not measure: where `block: 'start'` lands under the page's sticky chrome, whether the ring is visible, the lazy face against the 4 s settle, the phone row face, or an `html`/`richtext` body in the real view (that face is pinned only against hand-written DOM). No producer exists before cloud 10c, so no user reaches this path yet and it need not block; but the check should be written onto a card (#37487 or the 10c card) so it is done before 10c ships.

**6. Point (e): #37487 is the right carrier.** Open, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue`, `area:ai`, `Parent: #37365`; it names the three rebuild paths, asks a pin and a control per path, and says to land before 10c. See S3 for what the PR's own text should say meanwhile.

S3 (should-fix) — the docs and the changeset claim more than the head delivers. Both say an answer "now draws" its citations and that "the list is drawn as it was persisted". On this head no producer emits `data-record-citations` (the only hits on `main` are the spec's own declaration), and a persisted list is not redrawn after a reload (#37487). AGENTS.md rule 10 asks the claim to be as narrow as the enforcement, and the changeset sentence ships in `CHANGELOG.md`. Add one sentence to the changeset and the two doc pages: drawn for a live turn whose stream carries the part; not yet restored from history (#37487).

**7. Locales: clean.** `chatbot.recordCitations.title` is present once in each of the 11 locale files (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant), at the same place in the `chatbot` block. All ten non-English values are translated; es and pt-BR share the spelling `Citado de registros`, which is correct in both. It is the only user-facing string the diff adds.

**Nits.**
- N1 (nit) — `encodeURIComponent` leaves `.` and `..` whole, so a citation whose `object` or `id` is `..` yields a path with a dot segment. It stays same-origin under the console's routes and the page still authenticates; `open_record` on `main` has the same shape; and the list is verified server-side before it is persisted. `recordOpenTarget` could refuse the two values.
- N2 (nit) — `escapeAttr` escapes `"` and `\` only; `CSS.escape` is the complete form. Field names are metadata identifiers, so nothing reaches it today.
- N3 (nit) — `sectionCandidates` runs `headingsOf` over every long-text field on every render of `RecordDetailView` while `?section` is present. A `useMemo` on the record, the fields and the anchor would do.
- N4 (nit) — the card's 维护者速读 says a citation lists 记录名 + 摘句; the chip shows the quote alone, as the card's What #2 says. Two citations of different records are told apart only by their quotes. No name is available without a fetch, which ruling Q1 excludes.
- N5 (nit) — the PR body names `DetailSection.tsx` as the one file shared with #37436; the 11 locale files are shared too (disjoint). The claim amendment was posted after the push, not before.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/i18n`: correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). The four packages are exactly those whose `src` the diff moves. Both declaration lines stand at line start in the PR body and the changeset body and agree. `Clause-②: yes` is right: `section` is a new reserved console URL parameter and `onOpenRecord`'s argument gains an optional `anchor`; both are widenings, nothing is narrowed, and the record-link grammar is untouched (`recordLink.ts` is not in the diff). No spec file changed. Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- `security_findings: none`: agreed, with N1 and N2 as hardening notes.
- Deviation, files beyond the claim: answered in ① 4. Accepted.
- Deviation, browser NOT MEASURED: answered in ① 5 (S4). Accepted for this head, carrier owed.
- Deviation, full suites at `e581d1410`: answered in ① 5. Verified and moot.
- Deviation, PR footer form: no contract effect.
- Reading A2 "holds only in part": the fix taken is narrower than claimed (S1).
- Out-of-scope finding, chips lost on reload: carried by #37487. Accepted (S3 for the wording).
- SQL push-down: not touched. The diff adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the locator reads only the record the page already holds.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `60981028c1462e71f9b72f08ef312e4c0c0d98d8`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7186860933 (declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`) reads PASS, with four should-fix findings and no must-fix.

Security came out clean:
- The route is always `/apps/…/record/…`, with each segment encoded and the anchor in `URLSearchParams`.
- `section` is only compared with `===`, never put into a selector.
- The record route runs its normal read.
- `section` is declared in `RESERVED_URL_PARAMS`.

S1–S3 close in this PR before ACCEPT. S4 needs a named carrier.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 27 files (+1050/−14), `Clause-②: yes` (new reserved URL param `section`), `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch on four packages. Not governed. Check-runs: 52 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: `extractRecordCitations` reads through the spec schema, and a refused part draws nothing. The overlaps with #37436 (`DetailSection.tsx`, the 11 locales) are disjoint hunks and safe in either order. #37487 is the right carrier for the lost-on-reload case.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** `locateSection` can mark the wrong heading. The ordinal counts same-reading headings in the outline but indexes into the drawn face. Example: a setext, quoted, list or indented `Scope` before `# Scope` takes index 0. The reverse also happens: an outline-listed heading the face does not draw shifts the real one. Fix: carry the outline's same-reading count, and fall back to the field when the drawn count differs. Pin the setext-duplicate case. The "never a wrong heading" claim must then hold as written.
   - **S2.** `focusRecordSection`'s cleanup never removes the mark. A second chip for the same record with a different anchor leaves both headings marked. The same chip, clicked again after scrolling away, does nothing. Unmark on change and re-run on a repeat click, then pin both.
   - **S3.** The changeset and both doc pages say an answer "now draws" its citations "as persisted". Nothing on `main` emits the part (that is cloud 10c), and a reload does not redraw it (#37487). Narrow the wording. The changeset sentence ships in `CHANGELOG.md`.
   - **S4.** The browser check (scroll under sticky chrome, ring visibility, the lazy face against the 4 s settle, the phone row, `html`/`richtext` bodies) is NOT MEASURED and has no carrier. Add it to #37487's acceptance, or to the 10c card, by name. No user reaches this path before 10c.
   - The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations** (nits, record only):
   - N1: `..` segments stay same-origin, the same shape as `open_record` on `main`.
   - N2: `escapeAttr` is applied to a metadata field name. `CSS.escape` is better if cheap.
   - N3: `sectionCandidates` is not memoised.
   - N4: the card's 速读 wording.
   - N5: the PR body names only `DetailSection.tsx` as shared with #37436.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: chips lost on reload go to #37487 (p2, under #37365, lands before 10c). The browser check goes there or to 10c (S4).
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. Still owed: S1–S3 closed, S4 carried, a same-head delta PASS, and an **ACCEPT**. Then the area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c1b30e6a0b0c2548b331de1711581d9749459203`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: no

Delta round on PR #37485 (card #37365, epic #36996 row 10b), declaration face. It follows record 7186860933 on `60981028c` and seat REWORK 7186871392. Read this round: delta report 7190002779, `git diff 60981028c..c1b30e6a0b` (one commit, 10 files; no merge of `main` and no rebase, merge base still `5d21d431e`), the whole diff `origin/main...c1b30e6a0b` (27 files, +1274/−12), the patched PR body, card #37487 with its comments, and the head's check-runs. `main` has moved to `54ea3c8c38`; none of the files it changed since the merge base is in this PR. Nothing was built or run; every finding is a reading of the code, and none was reproduced.

### ① Derived judgments

**Verdict in one line:** no must-fix. S1, S2 and S3 are closed, S4 is carried on #37487, N2 and N3 are closed. The S2 fix opens one new should-fix (S5): the focus now re-runs when a navigation drops the history state.

**Earlier findings.**

S1 (should-fix) — CLOSED. `sectionCandidates` now puts the outline's `count` of same-reading headings on each candidate. `locateSection` takes `drawn[ordinal]` only when `drawn.length === candidate.count`, and opens the field for a candidate whose reading is empty. Both directions from the first round resolve to the field: a same-titled heading the outline does not list (setext, quoted, list, indented) makes the drawn count larger, and a listed heading the face does not draw makes it smaller. Pinned with controls in `recordSectionAnchor.test.tsx` (the same-titled unlisted heading, the listed undrawn heading for either anchor, the empty reading) and through the real view in `RecordDetailView.citedSection-37365.test.tsx`. The report's mutation (dropping the count check) turns three of them red. The PR body's A2 note no longer says "never". The residue is N6.

S2 (should-fix) — CLOSED, with S5 as its consequence. `markSection` returns an unmark that removes the attribute and only the classes it added; `focusRecordSection`'s cleanup calls it, so a second anchor on the same record leaves one mark. The chat opener passes a fresh `RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE` value on each chip click and `RecordDetailView` keys the effect on record, anchor and that value, so the same chip clicked again scrolls and marks again. Pinned in the helper test, the real-view test and `AiChatPage.recordLink-13037.test.tsx`. The key is history state, not a URL parameter (the `RECORD_COMMENTS_PUSHED_STATE` precedent), so `Clause-②` is unchanged and nothing joins `RESERVED_URL_PARAMS`.

S3 (should-fix) — CLOSED. The changeset title and body, `plugin-chatbot.mdx` and the chatbot `README.md` now say the console draws a verified citations part when a live answer carries one, that nothing in this release emits the part, and that a conversation reloaded from history does not redraw it yet. The changeset also states the new fallback (a different number of same-titled headings opens the field) and the moving mark.

S4 (should-fix) — CARRIED on #37487. Seat comment 7186889924 on that card adds the booted-console check to its acceptance: chips drawn, a chip click opening `?section=ANCHOR` with the cited heading in view and marked from the dock and `/ai`, the chips redrawn after a reload, a refused part drawing nothing. The PR body's verification line points there. That acceptance lives in a comment, not the card body, and does not name the sticky chrome, the phone row or an `html`/`richtext` body; whoever takes #37487 should read the comment as part of the card.

N1 (nit) — OPEN, accepted by the seat as a deviation. Dot segments in `object` or `id` are still not refused; same-origin, same shape as `open_record` on `main`.
N2 (nit) — CLOSED. `escapeAttr` uses `CSS.escape` when present.
N3 (nit) — CLOSED. The candidates are in a `useMemo` on the record, the fields and the anchor.
N4 (nit) — OPEN, accepted. The chip shows the quote alone.
N5 (nit) — CLOSED. The PR body now lists the locale overlap with #37436.

**New this round.**

S5 (should-fix) — a navigation that drops the history state re-opens the cited section. `citedSectionKey` ends in the `RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE` value, or `''` when the entry carries none. `RecordDetailView`'s own URL writes keep `location.state`, and the new CONTROL pins that case. Other writers on the same route do not: `useUrlOverlay` (`setSearchParams(sp, { replace })`, used by the command palette and the keyboard-shortcuts dialog), the record-form overlay in `AppContent.tsx` and `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx` (`setSearchParams(sp)`). On a record opened from a chip, opening the palette or the edit form changes the key from the click's value to `''`; the effect cleans up, unmarks and focuses again, so the page scrolls back to the cited heading behind the overlay. Closing the form with Back restores the entry that holds the value, and the page scrolls there once more. On the previous head the key was record and anchor only, so these writes moved nothing. Smallest fix: re-run only when a NEW string value arrives (hold the last value seen for this record and anchor, and ignore its absence), with a pin for a state-dropping replace and a push-then-back. No user reaches a chip before cloud 10c, so it need not block this head; close it here or name it on #37487.

N6 (nit) — the count check narrows S1's fault, it does not exclude it. A body with one same-titled heading the outline does not list AND one listed heading the face does not draw has equal counts and can still resolve to the other heading; so can a face that drew its headings one at a time. The markdown face draws in one commit, and the real-view pin holds. The PR body is worded correctly; the two test titles that say "never that heading" claim slightly more than the rule gives.

N7 (nit) — a heading with an empty reading opens the field only after the 4 s settle: `attempt` finishes at once for a `text` face but not for this case, though the answer is already known.

**Unchanged from the first round, re-read on this head.** Security is clean: `recordOpenTarget` is untouched, the new state value is a local counter string and never reaches a selector or markup, and the `section` value is still only compared with `===`. `Security-touching: no` stands: no changed hunk changes or teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. `section` remains the one new reserved parameter, declared in `urlParams.ts`. The plugin-chatbot, plugin-detail and i18n sources are byte-identical to `60981028c`, so the locale parity (11 of 11) and the overlap with #37436 stand as read.

**Check-runs on the head:** 66 completed, 54 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, as the area reports.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/i18n`: still correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (a new reserved URL parameter `section`)` stands at line start in the PR body and the changeset and the two agree. The delta adds no URL parameter and no public argument: `RECORD_SECTION_OPENED_STATE` is a history-state key, and `markSection`'s new return value is internal to app-shell. No spec file changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- `security_findings: none`: agreed.
- Deviation, N2 and N3 taken beyond the order: accepted; both are small and both are closed above.
- Deviation, the new history-state key: accepted as not a URL parameter; its side effect is S5.
- Deviation, worktree recreated at `60981028c`: no contract effect; the delta is one commit on that head.
- Reading A2: the PR body now states the rule and its limit without "never" (N6).
- Out-of-scope finding from round one, chips lost on reload: carried by #37487, which now also carries the browser check (S4).
- SQL push-down: not touched. The delta adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
